    All Classes and Interfaces

    Class
    Description
    Codec<A>
    How to write an A as JSON and read it back: a type class, resolved as a given.
    Codec.Encoder<T>
    A derived record's generated encoder: writes each field of value to out.
    Codec.Field<T,F>
    One component of a product: its JSON name, how to get it, and its codec.
    Codec.Out
    What a derived encoder writes to: the writer, plus the record's field names and codecs.
    FieldNames
    The field names of one shape, encoded once so readers and writers never build a String per field.
    ForjBackend
    forj's own JSON backend, with no third-party code: the default JsonBackend.
    Json
    Encoding and decoding whole documents.
    JsonBackend
    Makes readers and writers: the one thing a JSON parser plugs in.
    JsonException
    Malformed input, a value of the wrong kind, or a limit exceeded.
    JsonLimits
    Bounds a reader enforces, so hostile input can't exhaust the stack or the heap.
    JsonReader
    A pull reader over one JSON document, one token at a time.
    JsonToken
    What JsonReader.peek() sees next.
    JsonWriter
    A streaming writer for one JSON document.
    SealedCodec<T>
    Codec.sealed(String): a closed family of cases (a sealed interface and its records) as JSON objects that name their case in a discriminator field, written first: {"type":"card","number":"4111…"}.
    SealedCodec.Builder<T>
    Collects the cases; SealedCodec.Builder.build() makes the codec.
